description: The context graph for one product in one market, for every go-to-market job beyond the buyer list: short-form video ads, creator seeding, marketplace listings and images, trends and social listening, buyers, pricing and the rules before sale. Nodes are the facts each job must respect, taken from the same sources as gtm_plan: the market (UN Comtrade imports, growth, Korea's share, the industry's reply rate), the buyer types that reply, the creator platforms in order and each one's video format (aspect, length, safe zone, sound, AI-label rule), the marketplaces in order and each one's main-image rule, the outreach language, the everyday scene for visuals, the claims you can show or say, disclosure and AI-content rules, product rules and easy-to-miss requirements with official sources, the price ladder multiple, and the live-data signals to read before creating (trending hashtags, competitor ads, best-seller reviews, search demand). Edges link them (market → platform → format, market → marketplace, product → rules, signal → platform). Each job lists the nodes it uses, a short brief, read_first signal calls, the next tool call with ready arguments (video_studio, image_studio, channel_plan, gtm_plan, price_ladder, blind_spots), whether it is paid and its estimated cost, and wait_for_gate when an approval must come first. Rules come from the same export context as video_studio and image_studio (same sale gate, claims_check, and company when signed in), and each job reads the requirements that bind it, the easy-to-miss ones included: ad rules for video and seeding, rules for sending samples to creators and buyers (e.g. US Prior Notice covers food samples, alcohol cannot go by US mail, couriers for perfume and lithium batteries), listing and label rules plus what you take on when you sell direct by parcel without an importer (e.g. Japan's 24 units per item, an EU responsible operator, packaging EPR), prior consent for sales email, and extra duties or taxes for the price (check them against price_ladder's notes). The before-you-sell checks of gtm_plan reach the same jobs: file the trademark before ads, creator posts or listings show the brand, duty and proof of origin for the quote (in the US, quote the Section 301 rate even with a KORUS claim), and payment terms for first orders; Korea-only lines (Korean FTAs, K-SURE) are left out for products made outside Korea. rules_coverage says how much TradeGraph knows for that market (national, bloc, pointers or none: none is not a clearance), with official-source pointer nodes and where to check what is not on file; rules_page links the public page with the same rules and their official sources when there is one. Signed in, it starts from the company's own records (learned): the last market reads saved with company_context (kind=signal) sit on the signal nodes with their age and whether they are stale, so a fresh read is reused instead of paid for again; seeding_list results per platform (contacted, agreed, posted) sit on the platform nodes and the seeding brief; hook tests (kind=result: views and viewers past 2 seconds per angle) sit on the video format and brief, so the next video starts from the angle that held best. These are the company's own numbers only; nothing is shared with other companies. Call it after gtm_plan when the user wants to launch in a market ("what do we need for Japan", "make videos for TikTok in Vietnam", "list on Qoo10"), or before video_studio and image_studio so hooks and frames start from the market. Omit country to use the data's first market. job returns one job only. Free, read-only.

country.description: Target country as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g. 'US', 'JP') or an English/Korean name. Optional: omit to use the market the data picks first (the same as gtm_plan).

description.description: Optional: the product as the user describes it, any language (e.g. '비건 선크림 SPF50', '할랄 인증 저가 립스틱', 'premium anti-aging ampoule already on Amazon US'). Used to detect product traits that change the rules within one HS code (see traits) and the concepts, price tier, certifications and markets already selling that change which market fits (product_profile, entry_paths).

item.description: Product as an HS4 code (e.g. '3304') or a name in English or Korean (e.g. 'sunscreen', '라면'). Names cover TradeGraph's 35 items; any other product works as a 4-digit HS code (e.g. '1905' biscuits, '2005' kimchi, '3305' shampoo) with live UN Comtrade imports.

job.description: Optional: one job only (smaller answer). Default all.

product.description: Optional: the product in plain English as it looks or is sold (e.g. 'vegan sunscreen SPF50, 50 ml white tube'), passed on to the next calls.

traits.description: Optional: product traits, comma-separated, that change the rules within one HS code: sunscreen, whitening (also arbutin, kojic acid), vitamin_a (retinol), gel_nail (UV/LED gel, semi-cured strips), contact_lens (HS 9001: contact lenses, colour lenses), hair_dye, hair_loss, acne, antiperspirant, dandruff, fluoride (toothpaste), human_derived (human stem cell culture media, human placenta, cord blood: a ban in the EU, UK, China and ASEAN), stem_cell (stem cell culture media whose source is not named: check it), exosome, radio (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular), battery, meat, dairy, egg, aerosol, flammable, industrial or household (for HS codes that hold both, such as 8414 fans, compressors and vacuum pumps: picks machinery rules, trade fairs and buyer searches, or household-appliance ones). Also detected from item, product and description; the answer lists them in product_traits.

name: context_graph
title: Go-to-market context graph: every job in one market (video, creators, listings, buyers)
